turns.prompt_text: Can you find the instruction manual for this light switch Attached 1 file. - d49564aa-f4d5-43aa-ac94-88b72267e93b
turns.response_html:
Based on the image you provided, the light switch is a Legrand RIRW6000. It's a sensor switch that can be configured as either an occupancy or a vacancy sensor.

You can find the instruction manual for this device and similar models from Legrand on various websites. The manual will contain detailed information on installation, wiring, and how to set the various functions, such as time delay and operating mode.

Here's what you can expect to find in the manual:

  • Wiring Instructions: Diagrams and steps for connecting the switch in a single-pole or 3-way setup. It will explain which wire goes to the hot line, the load, the ground, and the traveler (runner) wires for multi-location installations.
  • Operating Modes: How to switch between occupancy mode (lights turn on and off automatically) and vacancy mode (lights must be turned on manually but will turn off automatically).
  • Time Delay Adjustment: Instructions on how to set the amount of time the lights stay on after no motion is detected.
  • Troubleshooting: Common issues and solutions, such as what to do if the lights don't turn on or if the sensor isn't working correctly.

turns.prompt_text: can you tell me what each colored wire represents
turns.response_html: Generally, black and red wires are hot (live current), white wires are neutral, and bare copper or green wires are ground. Yellow and blue wires can also be hot, particularly in specific switch configurations.

turns.prompt_text: can you tell me on my Legrand light switch what the yellow cable is
turns.response_html: The yellow wire on a Legrand RIRW6000 light switch is a traveler or signal wire. It is used for 3-way or multi-location configurations, connecting the switch to other compatible switches or radiant timers. In a single-pole setup, the yellow wire is usually capped and not used.
